label: Town
_model: The settlement kernel: the APPETITE belongs to the place, not to a buried person. A town wants to be prosperous, respectable, safe or necessary, and its ACCOMMODATION is what a corporation does to keep it that way — price people out, charter them away, wall them off. Claimants are offices, not corpses.

appeasement.move: pay a debt that is not yours, in public

appetites.purpose: nothing unseemly would ever be visible

appeasement.move: compliment the town on how well it is kept, in the street
submit to being searched, without complaint
appeasement.why: a stranger has been checked, properly

appetites.purpose: the road would always come through here
appetites.asks: "Where do you think you are going?"

appeasement.move: ask the town for directions, and take them
appeasement.why: the town was needed for something

accommodations.text: priced {conscript} out until they left of their own accord
chartered {conscript} away to another town entirely
walled {conscript} outside the gates and did not open them
indentured {conscript} to the corporation for three generations
struck {conscript} from the rolls, so the town could say they had never been here
housed {conscript} where they could not be seen from the square

charter.label: the charter that made the town rich
charter.function: the only proof the privilege was ever granted

portrait.label: the town's official portrait of itself
portrait.function: the version everyone agreed to remember

keys.label: the keys to the gates, all four
keys.function: the only things the walls answer to

milestone.label: the milestone that says all roads pass here

factions.name: the Corporation
factions.essence: still meeting, still minuting, still deciding

factions.name: the debtors
factions.essence: owed on and owing, and still here

factions.name: the Watch
factions.essence: checking papers nobody has issued for centuries

triggerGlossary.announced: came in by the main gate and paid the toll, publicly
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: noticed by two different windows, or a window and a watchman
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice in a public place — the town minds that
triggerGlossary.lingering: stood about in the square long enough to be asked your business
triggerGlossary.disturbed: moved something the Corporation had placed

skirmish.avoid: produce any document with a seal and they will accept it

fight.line: 4 Bandits and a Hobgoblin Soldier as sergeant

foes.name: Hobgoblin Soldier
foes.note: the others hold while he lasts

fight.avoid: drop the sergeant and the rest are Nerve 2

battle.line: 1 Necromancer of the Corporation and 4 Skeletons

foes.name: Necromancer
foes.note: raises one Skeleton per round from the paupers' ground

battle.harmedBy: anything — but the Skeletons keep coming until the Necromancer stops
battle.avoid: he is a clerk and will take a bribe, in coin, publicly

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith of the Mayor, 1 Necromancer and 5 Skeletons

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

ledger.dangerLine: the town is still owed, and it keeps very good records

institution: a debt-board in the square, names chalked and re-chalked
weights and measures chained to a bench, all of them shaved
a counting house with the shutters open at every hour
ritual: a market bell rung at an hour when nobody trades
accounts read aloud to an empty hall, quarterly
coins counted into a box that is already full
demand: a table set for a settlement, two chairs, one occupied
a room where a price is named before you ask
a hand out, palm up, at every doorway
wound: a ledger with a page cut out and the stub still in
houses emptied for arrears and never re-let
a debtor's stone worn hollow by kneeling
anchor: a charter under glass, the seal intact
a strongbox with one document and no coin
a tally-stick split and both halves kept

features: fresh chalk on a debt-board, this week's hand
a shop cleared out overnight and the door left open
coin scattered and not picked up, which never happens here
a stall taken down in a hurry, the frame still standing
a ledger left open at a page somebody wanted found
a lock changed on a door that was never locked

decisions.cue: a debt-board with a name you could pay off, or add to
decisions.cost: paying is public and generous; adding is quiet and cruel

resolve.success: you pay in the square and the Corporation counts you a benefactor
resolve.failure: your coin is refused as insufficient, publicly: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: walk past the board; nothing changes and nothing is owed

decisions.cue: a toll demanded at a gate by nobody in particular
decisions.cost: the toll is real even if the collector is not

resolve.success: you work out the correct toll from the board and pay exactly it — the gate opens
resolve.failure: you overpay and are marked as someone with money: every price rises for you
resolve.orElse: go round to the weighbridge: two Turns, no toll

decisions.cue: a set of shaved weights and a merchant about to use them
decisions.cost: exposing the fraud makes an enemy of the guild

resolve.success: you expose it in a way that flatters the Corporation's honesty and gain their favour
resolve.failure: you expose it clumsily and the guild closes ranks: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: say nothing; the merchant remembers your discretion

decisions.cue: a strongbox that opens to whoever holds the charter
decisions.cost: you do not hold the charter

resolve.success: you find the charter's copy in the muniment chest and the box opens
resolve.failure: the box holds and the attempt is entered in a ledger somewhere
resolve.orElse: break it: loud, roll the clock, contents damaged

decisions.cue: a debtor offering information for the price of their arrears
decisions.cost: their information is good; their arrears are not small

resolve.success: you settle the debt at a discount and get the whole of what they know
resolve.failure: you pay in full and they tell you half
resolve.orElse: refuse: they tell you nothing and follow you at a distance

decisions.cue: a tally-stick, split, with the other half somewhere in the town
decisions.cost: matching it proves a claim worth having

resolve.success: you match it against the counting-house half and hold a claim the town honours
resolve.failure: you match it wrongly and hold a claim on nothing: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it: no claim, no obligation

situations.doing: chalking a debt-board that has no room left
situations.onArrival: it asks whether you have come to settle
situations.because: the accounts must balance and never have
situations.offer: settle any debt at all and the whole board is wiped, which it badly wants

situations.doing: dividing a purse that is plainly not theirs
situations.onArrival: they stop and offer you a share
situations.because: they were paid to leave and could not
situations.offer: take the share and they will tell you who paid them

situations.doing: testing weights that are every one of them short
situations.onArrival: it hands you a weight and asks your honest opinion
situations.because: the measures must be certified and cannot be
situations.offer: certify them anyway and every trader in the town owes you

situations.doing: ringing an hour when no trade is permitted
situations.onArrival: the square begins, very slowly, to fill
situations.because: the hour was never struck from the calendar
situations.offer: trade something, anything, and the market recognises you as a burgess

situations.doing: counting coin into a box that is already full
situations.onArrival: it does not look up, and asks you to hold the lid
situations.because: the count has never once come out right
situations.offer: hold the lid and it will tell you which house the shortfall went to

situations.doing: waiting outside a door with a writ and no bailiff
situations.onArrival: they ask if you are going in anyway
situations.because: the writ cannot be served without an officer
situations.offer: serve it for them and they hand you what is behind the door

temptations.cue: a seal matrix for the town's charter
temptations.benefit: doors that check privilege open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the Corporation expects you at its next meeting

temptations.cue: half a split tally-stick
temptations.benefit: once, prove a debt is owed to you and be believed
temptations.standingDrawback: the other half is out there and its holder is looking

temptations.cue: a weight, subtly light
temptations.benefit: once, make a trade come out in your favour
temptations.standingDrawback: traders begin to check everything you hand them

temptations.cue: a writ of distraint, unserved, name blank
temptations.benefit: name someone and the Watch will detain them once
temptations.standingDrawback: your own name is on the reverse in the same clerk's hand

temptations.cue: a small key to a counting-house drawer
temptations.benefit: one locked box per scene opens
temptations.standingDrawback: the Corporation notices what has been opened

appearances.dangerLine: the town is being looked at, and it has arranged itself accordingly

institution: a square where every frontage is painted and every back is not
shutters on the side of the street the road can see
a fine hall with a fine door and no rooms behind it
ritual: a procession route swept daily, and only that route
a mayor's portrait unveiled every year to the same crowd
best clothes laid out in every house, for a visit that never comes
demand: a street arranged so a visitor is always in view
a mirror set at the end of the square, facing in
a bench positioned for being seen sitting on
wound: a row of houses with the fronts kept and the backs collapsed
a name painted over on a shopfront, badly
a portrait with one figure scraped out of the group
anchor: the town's own portrait of itself, framed and lit
a visitor's book with one page and many signatures
a plan of the town as it would like to be

features: fresh paint on one side of a street only
a curtain drawn across an alley mouth
a scandal-sheet trodden into the mud, still legible
a shopfront boarded and painted to look occupied
chairs set out in the square for an audience
a signboard taken down and the hooks left

decisions.cue: an alley the town would rather you did not walk down
decisions.cost: walking it sees what the frontage hides

resolve.success: you go down and back unobserved, and learn what the town is covering
resolve.failure: you are seen coming out of it: +1 Bane and the Corporation cools toward you
resolve.orElse: stay on the swept route: one Turn longer, no offence given

decisions.cue: a scandal-sheet naming somebody still influential here
decisions.cost: reading it aloud is a weapon; pocketing it is leverage

resolve.success: you use it to open a door that flattery alone would not
resolve.failure: you are seen holding it and become the story: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: burn it: the town relaxes and thanks you without saying so

decisions.cue: a group portrait with one figure scraped out
decisions.cost: asking who it was is a rude question here

resolve.success: you ask it delicately enough to be answered honestly
resolve.failure: you ask badly and the room closes: the next encounter starts hostile
resolve.orElse: do not ask; the gap goes unexplained and you are liked for it

decisions.cue: a procession forming that expects you to join or stand aside
decisions.cost: joining is endorsement; standing aside is comment

resolve.success: you join well and the town takes you for a person of standing
resolve.failure: you join badly and are laughed at: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: stand aside respectfully: neutral, and you lose one Turn

decisions.cue: a house-front with no house behind it, and a way through
decisions.cost: the way through is real; the pretence is what matters

resolve.success: you slip through without bringing the frontage down
resolve.failure: the frontage comes down, publicly: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: go round the block: one Turn

decisions.cue: a visitor's book open at a blank page
decisions.cost: signing puts you on the record, favourably or otherwise

resolve.success: you sign in a way that flatters the town and doors open
resolve.failure: you sign plainly and the town judges the hand: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it unsigned; you remain a stranger and are treated as one

situations.doing: painting a frontage that is already perfect
situations.onArrival: they ask you to stand back and judge the colour
situations.because: the street must look well from the road
situations.offer: approve the colour warmly and they will let you behind it

situations.doing: scraping a figure out of a group portrait
situations.onArrival: it pauses, brush up, and asks whether you know the face
situations.because: the town resolved that person had never been here
situations.offer: name the face and it will tell you what they did

situations.doing: sweeping a route that is already clean
situations.onArrival: it sweeps around you rather than asking you to move
situations.because: the route must be ready and the visit never comes
situations.offer: tell it the visitor has arrived and it will escort you anywhere

situations.doing: copying a notice down before it is taken away
situations.onArrival: they pocket the paper and smile at you carefully
situations.because: the story is real and the town is faster than they are
situations.offer: offer to distract the Beadle and they will share what they have

situations.doing: rehearsing a welcome to an empty square
situations.onArrival: it welcomes you instead, warmly and at length
situations.because: the speech has never once been given
situations.offer: let it finish and the town treats you as its guest of honour

situations.doing: standing in their best clothes at their doors
situations.onArrival: they nod as you pass, and keep standing
situations.because: word went round that someone important was coming
situations.offer: be that someone and every door on the street opens

temptations.cue: a small copy of the town's own portrait
temptations.benefit: show it and be taken for a person of standing
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected to behave like one, publicly

temptations.cue: a page torn from the visitor's book
temptations.benefit: once, be remembered as having been welcome here
temptations.standingDrawback: the page is missed, and the Corporation asks after it

temptations.cue: a scandal-sheet, folded small
temptations.benefit: once, make one person here do as you ask
temptations.standingDrawback: they will tell others what you are holding

temptations.cue: a good coat, cut for the square
temptations.benefit: the Watch does not stop you
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot be seen in the back lanes wearing it

temptations.cue: a pot of the town's own paint
temptations.benefit: once, make something look sound that is not
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever you painted will fail at the worst moment

vigilance.dangerLine: the town is still watching the road, and you came down it

institution: a gate that is shut at an hour nobody remembers agreeing
watch-boxes at every corner, all of them occupied
a wall built higher on the side facing the road
ritual: papers demanded at a gate that has no gatekeeper
a curfew bell rung to an empty street
a roll of strangers read out nightly
demand: a room you must be searched to leave
a bench where you are asked to wait and be looked at
a window arranged so the square can see who calls
wound: a gate barred from inside with the bar broken anyway
a list of strangers with every name struck through
a house burned deliberately, alone in its row
anchor: four gate-keys on one ring, hung where all can see
a strangers' book with the last entry unfinished
a bar for a gate, oiled, never used

features: a gate barred at midday, with no reason given
shutters closed on one house only
a watch-box with the brazier still warm
chalk marks on doors, recent, in a code
a barricade half-built across a lane
a dog kennel, empty, chain snapped

decisions.cue: a watchman demanding papers you do not have
decisions.cost: any document with a seal will do, if given confidently

resolve.success: you produce something and it is accepted; the Watch passes you through
resolve.failure: your papers are refused and you are entered in the strangers' book: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: go over the wall by the tannery: one Turn and a Brawn roll

decisions.cue: a gate shut against the hour, and a wicket beside it
decisions.cost: the wicket admits one person at a time

resolve.success: you work out the wicket's trick and the party passes one by one, unremarked
resolve.failure: the wicket sticks and the noise brings the Watch: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: wait for the gate to open on the bell: two Turns

decisions.cue: a search you can submit to, or refuse
decisions.cost: submitting means showing what you carry

resolve.success: you submit and the Watch counts you honest — no further checks this delve
resolve.failure: you refuse and are followed for the rest of the delve
resolve.orElse: let them search only one of you: partial trust, one Turn

decisions.cue: chalk marks on doors in a code the Watch uses
decisions.cost: reading it tells you which houses are being watched

resolve.success: you read the code and know which doors are safe to knock at
resolve.failure: you copy a mark wrongly onto yourselves without realising
resolve.orElse: ignore the marks; knock and find out

decisions.cue: a curfew bell about to ring
decisions.cost: being on the street after it is an offence here

resolve.success: you talk your way into a doorway before it rings and are sheltered
resolve.failure: you are caught out after curfew: +1 Bane and the Watch escorts you
resolve.orElse: run for the gate: one Turn, loud, roll the clock

decisions.cue: a strangers' book with your description already in it
decisions.cost: somebody entered you before you arrived

resolve.success: you find who wrote it and what else they wrote
resolve.failure: you alter the entry and the alteration is noticed: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; the Watch has your description and uses it

situations.doing: checking papers nobody has carried for a century
situations.onArrival: it puts out a hand and waits
situations.because: the order to stand the watch was never rescinded
situations.offer: hand it anything with a seal and it will wave you through and salute

situations.doing: reading a roll of strangers aloud in an empty street
situations.onArrival: it reaches a blank and looks up at you
situations.because: the roll must be complete before the gate may open
situations.offer: give it names — any names — and the gate opens

situations.doing: waiting for the curfew bell before moving a crate
situations.onArrival: they put a finger to their lips and shrug
situations.because: the Watch is predictable and they are patient
situations.offer: help them shift it and they show you the way through the wall

situations.doing: closing itself, slowly, on no schedule you can see
situations.onArrival: the bar begins to slide across
situations.because: the hour was set by a council that no longer sits
situations.offer: hold the bar and it will stay open behind you

situations.doing: turning out a bag that keeps refilling
situations.onArrival: it asks you to empty your pockets, apologetically
situations.because: the search must be thorough and never is
situations.offer: let it search you properly and the Watch leaves you alone thereafter

situations.doing: standing at a corner, facing outward
situations.onArrival: they part to let you through without being asked
situations.because: something is expected from the road and it is not you
situations.offer: ask what they are watching for and they will tell you exactly

temptations.cue: one of the four gate-keys
temptations.benefit: one gate per scene opens for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the Watch counts the keys nightly and one is missing

temptations.cue: a set of papers with a good seal and a blank name
temptations.benefit: pass any check in the town without a roll
temptations.standingDrawback: you must answer to the name you wrote

temptations.cue: a scrap listing the chalk-code
temptations.benefit: once, know exactly which house is watched
temptations.standingDrawback: you begin marking doors yourself without noticing

temptations.cue: a hand-bell from a watch-box
temptations.benefit: ring it and the street empties for one scene
temptations.standingDrawback: the Watch comes to see who rang

temptations.cue: a page of the strangers' book
temptations.benefit: once, prove you were here all along
temptations.standingDrawback: someone else's alibi is now missing

thoroughfare.dangerLine: the town needs the road to come through it, and will arrange that

institution: milestones all pointing here, some of them moved
a bridge that is the only bridge for a day's ride
roads that all bend, slightly, toward the square
ritual: a toll taken at a bar that swings on nothing
carts waved through by a hand at a window
a road swept before a coach that never comes
demand: a market you must cross to get anywhere at all
a square with one exit visible and three not
a street that returns you to where you started
wound: a rival town's milestone, broken and kept
a road washed out and never repaired, deliberately
a bypass surveyed, staked, and the stakes pulled up
anchor: the milestone that says all roads pass here
a map with one road drawn heavier than the rest
a bridge-toll board, the figures freshly cut

features: a signpost turned to point the wrong way
a road newly blocked with a felled tree
cart-ruts that stop in the middle of a field
a bridge plank taken up and laid beside the gap
survey stakes pulled up and stacked
a milestone with the distance recut

decisions.cue: a signpost that has plainly been turned
decisions.cost: following it goes somewhere the town wants you to go

resolve.success: you read the wear on the post and work out the true direction
resolve.failure: you follow it and lose a Turn, arriving where the town intended
resolve.orElse: ask a local: they will tell you truly, and the town will know you asked

decisions.cue: a toll-bar across the only bridge
decisions.cost: the toll is small; the record of paying it is not

resolve.success: you pay and are entered as legitimate traffic — the town stops obstructing you
resolve.failure: you argue the toll and the bar stays down: lose a Turn, +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: ford it downstream: one Turn, everything gets wet

decisions.cue: a market you must cross, and it does not want you to cross quickly
decisions.cost: the crowd is the obstacle and it is deliberate

resolve.success: you move through by seeming to belong, and are not delayed
resolve.failure: you are drawn into three transactions and lose a Turn
resolve.orElse: go round by the back lanes: one Turn, and you are noticed doing it

decisions.cue: survey stakes for a bypass, pulled up and stacked
decisions.cost: replanting them is a declaration of war on the town

resolve.success: you replant enough to matter and the surveyors' ghosts owe you
resolve.failure: you are seen at it: the Corporation treats you as hostile from here
resolve.orElse: leave them stacked; the bypass stays unbuilt

decisions.cue: a square with three exits and only one that leaves
decisions.cost: the other two return you here

resolve.success: you spot which street the ruts actually leave by
resolve.failure: you take a returning street: lose a Turn and roll the clock
resolve.orElse: follow a cart out: whichever way it goes, one Turn

decisions.cue: a milestone recut to move the town closer to everywhere
decisions.cost: correcting it is honest and unwelcome

resolve.success: you read the older cut beneath and know the true distances
resolve.failure: you accept the new figures and misjudge your time: lose a Turn
resolve.orElse: take the milestone at its word and hurry

situations.doing: raising a bar that hangs on nothing at all
situations.onArrival: it names a toll and waits, hand out
situations.because: the bridge must be paid for and the bridge is gone
situations.offer: pay anything and it will tell you the true road

situations.doing: arguing with a signpost that has been turned
situations.onArrival: they appeal to you as a witness
situations.because: they have been round this way three times
situations.offer: settle the argument and they will carry you a stage

situations.doing: staking out a bypass that the town keeps pulling up
situations.onArrival: it hands you the mallet without looking
situations.because: the survey must be completed and never is
situations.offer: drive one stake and it will show you the shortest way through

situations.doing: recutting a milestone, closer
situations.onArrival: they stand in front of the figures as you approach
situations.because: the distances must favour the town
situations.offer: admire the work and they will tell you the real distance, privately

situations.doing: filling a square that was empty a moment ago
situations.onArrival: it closes gently around you and does not let you hurry
situations.because: the market must be busy when strangers pass
situations.offer: buy something and the crowd opens

situations.doing: holding itself up on a span that is not there
situations.onArrival: the planks settle as you step on
situations.because: the crossing must exist because the charter says so
situations.offer: cross confidently and it holds; hesitate and it does not

temptations.cue: a milestone small enough to carry
temptations.benefit: once, make a journey shorter than it is
temptations.standingDrawback: distances you did not carry get longer

temptations.cue: a toll-board with the figures cut
temptations.benefit: once, demand passage and be given it
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected to keep the bridge in repair

temptations.cue: a map with one road drawn heavier
temptations.benefit: never lose your way in the town
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot see the roads it leaves out

temptations.cue: a length of toll-bar, iron-shod
temptations.benefit: once, close a way behind you that nothing can pass
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever you shut out waits at that spot

temptations.cue: a carter's whip, worn to the handle
temptations.benefit: once, make anything give way and let you through
temptations.standingDrawback: the town treats you as traffic, not a guest
